note: £1,641 was the published headline at the 2023 TDCV (2,700 kWh electricity, 11,500 kWh gas). £1,477 is the same cap restated at the 2026 TDCV (2,500 / 9,500 kWh), read from page 3 of the July summary letter https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/sites/default/files/2026-06/Summary-of-changes-to-energy-price-cap-1-July-to-30-September-2026.pdf. quantity: Ofgem price cap, typical dual-fuel Direct Debit annual bill, 1 July - 30 September 2026

Headline is £1,663 at the new TDCV (+13% vs £1,477 restated Apr-Jun); £1,862 at the old 2023 TDCV. DD unit rates (https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/news/changes-energy-price-cap-between-1-july-and-30-september-2026): electricity 26.11p/kWh, SC 57.19p/day; gas 7.33p/kWh, SC 29.04p/day (incl. 5% VAT). quantity: Ofgem price cap, typical dual-fuel Direct Debit annual bill, 1 October - 31 December 2026
title: Energy price cap (default tariff) update from 1 October 2026 (26 August 2026); press release 'Energy price cap will rise by 4% from October 2026'
note: At 2026 TDCV (2,500 kWh electricity, 9,500 kWh gas); +4% (+£60) on £1,663. £1,935 at the old 2023 TDCV is from the press release https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/press-release/energy-price-cap-will-rise-4-october-2026 . Reflects 0% VAT on domestic electricity from 1 Oct 2026 to 31 Mar 2027 (gas stays at 5%); Ofgem says the cap would be around £45 higher without it. DD unit rates (https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/news/changes-energy-price-cap-between-1-october-and-31-december-2026): electricity 26.32p/kWh excl. VAT, SC 54.83p/day; gas 7.97p/kWh, SC 29.68p/day (incl. 5% VAT). Other methods: standard credit £1,861, PPM £1,678, E7 DD £1,046. Ofgem will announce the Jan-Mar 2027 cap by 25 November 2026, so it is not yet published.

quantity: Average weekly household expenditure on electricity (all UK households)
title: Family spending workbook 1: detailed expenditure and trends, FYE 2025, Table A1, line 4.4.1 (released 11 June 2026)
note: Living Costs and Food Survey (~5,000 households). Table A1 numbers its categories sequentially: 4.4.1 Electricity, which is not the COICOP 4.5.1 code (ONS: 'The numbering is sequential, it does not use actual COICOP codes'). This is an average over all households, including non-recording ones (4,940 of 5,000 recorded). Aggregate £574m per week. Percentage standard error 1.1%. Times 52 = £1,040 per year (my derivation). Covers April 2024 to March 2025, when prices were lower than 2026 cap levels. Bulletin: https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/personalandhouseholdfinances/expenditure/bulletins/familyspendingintheuk/april2024tomarch2025

quantity: Number of domestic gas meters

quantity: Share of domestic properties not connected to the gas grid
title: Subnational electricity and gas consumption summary report 2024, section 4

quantity: RF targeted energy discount: share of households eligible under a £24,000 highest-individual-income threshold (plus means-tested benefit passporting)
title: Billing me softly (10 August 2026)
note: All values 'around'. The report states 75% coverage of the poorest four deciles of equivalised AHC income; the press release (https://www.resolutionfoundation.org/press-releases/government-must-be-ready-to-provide-targeted-energy-support-if-further-price-spikes-cause-more-families-to-struggle-this-winter/) states 83% of the poorest fifth. These are different populations, not a contradiction. Eligibility is tested on taxable income, while deciles use HBAI AHC income, so coverage is below 100% even in the poorest decile. The alternative total household income test (under £30,000, OECD BHC-equivalised) also reaches about 40% of households. Source data: RF analysis of the FRS, GB, 2024-25.

quantity: RF targeted energy discount: scheme cost and average discount per eligible household
title: Billing me softly (10 August 2026)
note: Delivered as a unit-rate discount on gas and electricity, so the value varies with consumption. £175 is the average over eligible households. The tiered amounts are 'around' values within the same £2bn envelope. RF says the cost should be met from public funds, not a bill levy. Implied eligible households at £2bn / £175 is about 11.4 million (my derivation, not stated by RF).

quantity: RF contextual figures: passporting reach, 2022 universal support cost, VAT cut value, gas-grid share, composition effects
title: Billing me softly (10 August 2026)
note: Passporting reach is stated as 'around a quarter' of British households. The VAT figure (about £45 a year) matches Ofgem's statement for the Oct-Dec 2026 cap. Of the 490,000 working-age couples with children who lose out, 71% are in the poorest fifth; of the 780,000 pensioner households who gain, 81% (630,000) are in decile five or above. Also stated: more than 15% of second-quintile households could not afford to keep their home warm in 2022-23. The press release says 'second income quartile', but the report says quintile.
